settings.heading: Where to sell what, and why the same item performs differently on each platform
settings.body: The product isn't the only variable. The same pack of earrings can fly on one platform and sit dead on another, purely because of who is browsing and how that platform decides what to show them. Here's how the four main UK platforms actually behave.

settings.heading: Match the product to the buyer's mood, not just the category
settings.body:
Every platform attracts people in a particular frame of mind. Someone on eBay usually knows what they want and is comparing prices. Someone on TikTok Shop wasn't shopping at all until three seconds ago. Someone on Vinted is browsing for pleasure, in a fashion mindset, expecting a bargain.

Get this right and everything else — pricing, photos, titles — becomes easier. Get it wrong and no amount of good listing writing rescues it.

settings.heading: The four that matter in the UK
settings.body: Read these as tendencies, not laws. Test with a small batch before you commit a whole pack to one platform.

settings.label: VINTED
settings.heading: Fashion, accessories and jewellery — browsing buyers
settings.body:
Best for: clothing, jewellery, hair accessories, bags, small fashion items. Anything that photographs well and reads as a treat.

Why it works: no seller fees, huge UK audience, and buyers who browse for enjoyment rather than hunting a specific item. Impulse-friendly price points (roughly £5–£25) move fastest.

Watch out for: buyers expect bargains and will haggle. Build your floor price in before you list. Vinted is also the platform most likely to flag accounts that look like scaled reselling — pace your listings and read the Safety Guide before you scale.

Avoid: electronics and bulky homeware. Wrong audience entirely.

settings.label: EBAY
settings.heading: Electronics, brands and anything people search by name — intent buyers
settings.body:
Best for: electronics, gadgets, tools, homeware, and any product with a model name or number people type into a search box.

Why it works: buyers arrive with intent. They already want the thing; they're deciding who to buy it from. That means less persuasion and more competition on price, postage speed and feedback score.

Watch out for: seller fees take a real bite — build them into your break-even before you list, not after. Your feedback score matters enormously early on, so your first ten orders are worth over-delivering on.

Strength: the sold-listings filter is the single best free demand-research tool in reselling. Use it before you buy stock, not after.

settings.label: TIKTOK SHOP
settings.heading: Visual, demonstrable products — discovery buyers
settings.body:
Best for: anything that looks good in motion or has a visible before-and-after. Ring lights, gadgets, beauty accessories, novelty homeware, jewellery with sparkle.

Why it works: nobody arrives intending to buy. The video creates the want and the checkout is one tap away. A single video that lands can clear a whole pack in a day.

Watch out for: it is content work, not listing work. You need to keep posting, and most videos do nothing. Treat it as a channel that occasionally spikes rather than a steady earner.

Avoid: anything that needs explaining in writing or looks flat on camera.

settings.label: FACEBOOK MARKETPLACE
settings.heading: Bulk, bundles and local pickup — practical buyers
settings.body:
Best for: homeware, larger items, job lots and bundles. Also the best place to shift the tail end of a pack that's stopped moving elsewhere.

Why it works: no fees, local collection removes postage costs entirely, and buyers are comfortable with bundles rather than single items.

Watch out for: more time-wasters than anywhere else. Expect messages that go nowhere and people who don't turn up. Never take payment methods you can't verify, and meet in public places.

Strength: genuinely useful as a clearance channel so old stock doesn't tie up your cash.

settings.label: JEWELLERY & ACCESSORIES
settings.heading: Vinted first, TikTok Shop second
settings.body: Photographs well, sits at an impulse price, and Vinted's audience is already in a fashion mindset. Use TikTok Shop for the pieces with visible sparkle or movement.

settings.label: ELECTRONICS
settings.heading: eBay first, TikTok Shop second
settings.body: People search electronics by name, which is eBay's home ground. Anything demonstrable — ring lights, earbuds — is worth filming for TikTok Shop too.

settings.label: FASHION
settings.heading: Vinted, then Marketplace for the leftovers
settings.body: Vinted is the fashion platform in the UK. When a size or colour stops moving, bundle the remainder onto Facebook Marketplace rather than sitting on it.

settings.label: HOME & LIFESTYLE
settings.heading: Marketplace and eBay
settings.body: Bulkier items where postage hurts your margin do better with local collection. Candles and giftable items also lift sharply in the run-up to Christmas.

settings.label: STARTER BOXES
settings.heading: Split them across two platforms
settings.body: A mixed box is a free experiment. List half on one platform and half on another, then reorder toward whichever cleared faster. That's real data on your own audience.

settings.label: ANY CATEGORY
settings.heading: Check demand before you buy
settings.body: Search the item on eBay and filter to sold listings. If similar items sold in the last month at a price above your break-even, there's demand. If not, no listing skill will fix it.

settings.heading: How to pick a platform for a new pack

settings.text: Search the item on eBay and filter to sold listings. This tells you whether anyone is buying it at all, and at what price.
Work out your true break-even: pack cost ÷ units, plus packaging, plus platform fees.
Match the product to the buyer mindset above. Browsing and fashion goes to Vinted; searched-for and technical goes to eBay.
List a small batch first — five or six units, not the whole pack. You're testing, not committing.
Give it a fortnight. Track views and saves as well as sales: lots of views and no sales usually means price, few views usually means title or keywords.
Put the rest where the test worked. If nothing moved anywhere, bundle onto Facebook Marketplace to release the cash and learn from it.
